branches.behavior: Return TRUNC(docdate): docdate converted to its local date in America/Los_Angeles, then cast back to timestamptz at local midnight.
branches.condition: No C_PaymentTerm row with C_PaymentTerm_ID = paymentterm_id (including paymentterm_id NULL)

branches.behavior: FirstDay = local date of docdate truncated to the month (date_trunc('month') on the LA-local timestamp, cast to date), then cast to timestamptz at local midnight on the 1st. NoDays = EXTRACT(day FROM TRUNC(docdate) - FirstDay). This is timestamptz - timestamptz, which gives a justify_hours'ed interval. Across the March DST start, e.g. 14 days minus 1 hour becomes '13 days 23:00', so NoDays is the local day-of-month minus 2 instead of minus 1. DueDate = adddays(FirstDay, FixMonthDay-1), i.e. FirstDay + (FixMonthDay-1)*86400 real seconds, with no clamping (day 31 in February spills into March). Then DueDate = DueDate + interval '1 month' * trunc(FixMonthOffset), where trunc goes toward zero; wall-clock time is kept and the day clamped to month end. Then, if NoDays > FixMonthCutoff (NULL cutoff means false), DueDate = DueDate + interval '1 month' again. This is a separate step, so clamping can happen twice.
branches.condition: Row found and IsDueFixed = 'Y' (exact uppercase; character(1) comparison)

branches.behavior: DueDate = adddays(TRUNC(docdate), NetDays) = local midnight of docdate + NetDays*86400 real seconds. NULL NetDays gives NULL.
branches.condition: Row found and IsDueFixed is anything other than 'Y' ('N', NULL, 'y', etc.)

response.date_time_semantics: Every step runs in the session TimeZone, America/Los_Angeles. TRUNC(timestamptz) = CAST(ts AS DATE) using the LA local date, then implicit date→timestamptz at LA local midnight. TRUNC(ts,'MM') casts to a timestamp without time zone in LA local time, takes date_trunc('month'), casts to date, then gets assigned to a timestamptz variable at LA midnight on the 1st. The '+ numeric' operator here is NOT date + integer. It is the custom adempiere operator timestamptz + numeric → adddays, which adds exact elapsed seconds. Starting from local midnight, crossing the spring-forward change (2nd Sunday of March) gives 01:00 local. Crossing fall-back (1st Sunday of November) gives 23:00 local on the PREVIOUS calendar day. add_months uses timestamptz + interval 'N months': convert to LA local time, add months to the year/month, clamp the day to the target month's length, keep the wall-clock time (00:00, 01:00, 23:00, etc.), and convert back to an instant using LA rules. PostgreSQL resolves a nonexistent local time (spring-forward gap) by moving it forward. It reads an ambiguous one (01:00 on fall-back day) as standard time (PST, the later instant). The NoDays difference is timestamptz - timestamptz, which PostgreSQL computes as microseconds and normalizes with justify_hours into days plus a sub-day time. So in March, after the DST start inside the month, the day count is one lower than the calendar difference. In November it isn't, because the extra hour just shows up as 01:00.
edge_cases: paymentterm_id = 106 (NetDays 30, IsDueFixed N), docdate 2026-11-19 10:00 PST: expect 2026-12-19 00:00 PST. No DST crossing.
Non-fixed, NetDays 30, docdate 2026-10-20 (PDT): local midnight + 30*86400s crosses the Nov 1 fall-back, giving 2026-11-18 23:00 PST, not 11-19 00:00.
Non-fixed, NetDays 30, docdate 2026-02-20 (PST): crosses the Mar 8 spring-forward, giving 2026-03-22 01:00 PDT.
paymentterm_id 105 (NetDays 0, fix* NULL): returns TRUNC(docdate), local midnight.
paymentterm_id not present (e.g. 999) or NULL: returns TRUNC(docdate), not NULL.
docdate NULL: returns NULL whether or not the term exists.
docdate given in UTC near midnight, e.g. 2026-11-20 05:00+00 = 2026-11-19 21:00 PST: the truncation uses the LA date, 11-19.

Fixed branch with FixMonthDay 15, offset 1, cutoff 10, docdate 2026-03-12: NoDays across the Mar 8 DST start is EXTRACT(day FROM '10 days 23:00') = 10, so 10 > 10 is false and no extra month. A naive port computes 11 and adds a month.

Fixed branch, docdate in November after the fall-back with FixMonthDay 15: FirstDay Nov 1 00:00 PDT + 14*86400s = Nov 14 23:00 PST, so the due day is the 14th (then shifted by months, keeping 23:00 wall time).
Fixed branch, FixMonthDay 31 and docdate in February: adddays spills into March 3/4 with no clamping. Then add_months clamps only if the target month is short.
Fixed branch, FixMonthDay 0: FirstDay - 1 day gives the last day of the previous month.
Fixed branch, January with FixMonthDay 31, offset 1, NoDays > cutoff: Jan 31 +1 month = Feb 28, then +1 month = Mar 28 (not Mar 31). Clamping happens twice.
Fixed branch, FixMonthCutoff NULL: never adds the extra month. FixMonthOffset NULL or FixMonthDay NULL: result NULL.
Fixed branch, FixMonthOffset 1.9 → 1 month; -0.5 → 0 months (truncate toward zero).
IsDueFixed lowercase 'y' or NULL: takes the NetDays branch.
Fractional NetDays 0.5: result is local noon (11:00/13:00 if crossing DST).
Fixed result whose wall time is 01:00 landing on the November fall-back day after add_months: ambiguous local time, which PostgreSQL resolves as PST.

inputs.meaning: C_PaymentTerm primary key to look up.
inputs.name: paymentterm_id
inputs.null_behavior: NULL matches no row (= NULL is never true). The loop body never runs and the function returns TRUNC(docdate).

inputs.meaning: Document date. Only its local calendar date in America/Los_Angeles matters, because it is truncated to local midnight.
inputs.name: docdate
inputs.null_behavior: TRUNC(NULL) is NULL. So DueDate starts NULL, and both branches give NULL (FirstDay is NULL, adddays/add_months return NULL). The result is NULL.

response.null_semantics: docdate NULL → NULL. paymentterm_id NULL or not found → TRUNC(docdate). IsDueFixed NULL → the NetDays branch, because NULL = 'Y' is not true. NetDays NULL (non-fixed branch) → NULL, because adddays returns NULL. FixMonthDay NULL → FixMonthDay-1 is NULL, adddays returns NULL, and the result is NULL. FixMonthOffset NULL → add_months returns NULL → NULL. FixMonthCutoff NULL → NoDays > NULL is NULL, so the IF is false and no extra month is added; this is not NULL. Fixed-branch columns are ignored in the non-fixed branch (e.g. row 105 has NULL fix* columns and NetDays 0, giving TRUNC(docdate)). NetDays is ignored in the fixed branch.

output.meaning: Due date as an absolute instant. Usually local midnight in America/Los_Angeles, but it can be 23:00 or 01:00 local, or a fractional time, because of second-based day arithmetic across DST changes or fractional day counts.
output.null_behavior: NULL if docdate is NULL. In the fixed branch: NULL if FixMonthDay or FixMonthOffset is NULL. In the non-fixed branch: NULL if NetDays is NULL. A NULL FixMonthCutoff does NOT give NULL; it just skips the extra month. No matching row returns TRUNC(docdate), not NULL.

porting_risks: Using calendar-day arithmetic (date + timedelta(days=n), or adding days to a local naive datetime) instead of exact elapsed seconds. The oracle drifts to 23:00 or 01:00 across DST and can roll back a whole calendar day in the fixed branch.
Treating '+ p.NetDays' as PostgreSQL's built-in date + integer. Operator resolution picks adempiere.adddays (timestamptz + numeric).
Doing the date work in UTC or the server's local zone instead of America/Los_Angeles. The truncation, month truncation, month addition and DST behavior all depend on the session TimeZone.
Computing NoDays as (date - first_of_month).days. The oracle uses a justify_hours'ed timestamptz interval, so in March after the DST start it is one less.
Using dateutil relativedelta(months=a+b) in one step. The oracle adds the offset months and the cutoff month separately, so clamping happens twice; it also keeps a non-midnight wall time.
Clamping FixMonthDay to the month length (a modern 'fix'). The oracle adds days with no clamping, so day 31 in February overflows into March.

Rounding instead of truncating FixMonthOffset, or truncating NetDays/FixMonthDay to integers. The oracle truncates the months toward zero (Python int() matches; math.floor does not for negatives) and honors fractional days.
Returning NULL when the term is not found. The oracle returns TRUNC(docdate).
Making a NULL FixMonthCutoff propagate NULL, or raising on it. The oracle just skips the extra month.
Comparing IsDueFixed case-insensitively or stripping/normalizing it. Only exact 'Y' selects the fixed branch.
Returning a naive datetime or a date. Output must be a tz-aware instant equal to the PostgreSQL timestamptz.

Resolving ambiguous or nonexistent local times differently from PostgreSQL. Python zoneinfo uses fold=0 (the earlier, PDT instant) by default, while PostgreSQL reads ambiguous times as standard time (fold=1) and moves gap times forward.
Microsecond precision: fractional days go through float8 and are rounded to microseconds. Use the same float math to match exactly.
Sample data only has IsDueFixed='N'. The fixed branch is untested by the live rows, so it needs synthetic rows for testing.
response.rounding_semantics: Days are added as seconds: interval '1 second' * (86400 * days). The numeric product is cast to float8 for interval * float8, and the resulting interval is rounded to microseconds. So fractional NetDays or FixMonthDay are honored as fractional days (e.g. NetDays 1.5 gives 36 hours later, local noon or 11:00/13:00 across DST). Nothing rounds them to whole days. FixMonthOffset goes through pg_catalog trunc(numeric), which truncates toward zero (2.9→2, -1.5→-1) before multiplying interval '1 month'. NoDays comes from EXTRACT(day ...) on the interval: it is the integer days field after justify_hours, which effectively floors, not rounds, the elapsed hours/24. FixMonthCutoff is compared as numeric, so a fractional cutoff works (NoDays 10 > 9.5 is true).
response.summary: Returns a payment due date for a payment term and a document date. It reads the single C_PaymentTerm row whose C_PaymentTerm_ID = paymentterm_id. Every date step is evaluated in the session TimeZone, America/Los_Angeles. (1) If no row matches, including when paymentterm_id is NULL, it returns TRUNC(docdate): local midnight of docdate as a timestamptz. (2) If IsDueFixed = 'Y': take FirstDay = local midnight on the 1st of docdate's month. NoDays = EXTRACT(day FROM (TRUNC(docdate) - FirstDay)). DueDate = FirstDay + (FixMonthDay-1) days, then add FixMonthOffset months, then add 1 more month if NoDays > FixMonthCutoff. (3) Any other IsDueFixed value, including NULL or lowercase 'y': DueDate = TRUNC(docdate) + NetDays days. 'Add N days' goes through the custom adempiere operator timestamptz + numeric, which calls adddays and adds 86400*N real seconds, not calendar days. So results that cross a DST change land at 23:00 or 01:00 local time. In the fixed branch this can even move the result to the previous calendar day. 'Add months' uses add_months, which is PostgreSQL timestamptz + interval 'N months': local wall-clock time is kept and the day is clamped to the month's last day. The local variable Days is declared but never used.

cases.rationale: 05:00 UTC is 21:00 on the previous day in LA, so truncation must use the LA date (11-19), giving 12-19 00:00 PST.

cases.name: fixed_march_dst_nodays
cases.rationale: The justify_hours interval across the DST start gives NoDays 10, not 11. With cutoff 10 no extra month is added: 2026-04-15 00:00 PDT.

cases.name: fixed_november_after_fallback
cases.rationale: Nov 1 00:00 PDT + 14*86400s = Nov 14 23:00 PST, so the due date lands on the 14th, not the 15th.

cases.name: fixed_day31_february_spill
cases.rationale: Day 31 in February is added as days with no clamping and spills to Mar 3, crossing no DST change (Mar 3 < Mar 8).

cases.name: fixed_day0_prev_month_end
cases.rationale: FixMonthDay 0 gives the last day of the previous month (Apr 30), then +1 month = May 30, not May 31.

cases.name: fixed_double_clamp
cases.rationale: Jan 31 +1 month = Feb 28, then the cutoff month gives Mar 28 (clamped twice), not Mar 31.

cases.name: fixed_cutoff_null
cases.rationale: A NULL cutoff skips the extra month and does not propagate NULL.

cases.name: fixed_offset_null
cases.rationale: A NULL FixMonthOffset makes add_months return NULL.

cases.name: fixed_offset_negative_fraction
cases.rationale: Offset -1.5 truncates toward zero to -1 month (floor would give -2).

cases.name: lowercase_y_uses_netdays
cases.rationale: Lowercase 'y' is not 'Y', so the NetDays branch runs (NetDays 10), not the fixed branch.

cases.name: isduefixed_null_fractional_netdays
cases.rationale: A NULL flag takes the NetDays branch. NetDays 0.5 gives local noon, so a port must not truncate fractional days.

cases.name: netdays_null

cases.name: fixed_ambiguous_fallback_0100
cases.rationale: Fractional day 1+1/24 gives Oct 1 01:00 PDT. +1 month = Nov 1 01:00, which is ambiguous; PG resolves it as PST (fold=1), while zoneinfo defaults to PDT.

cases.name: fixed_leap_year_day30
cases.rationale: Feb 2028 is a leap month: Feb 1 + 29 days = Feb 30 overflow lands on Mar 1, not Mar 2.

cases.name: fixed_fractional_cutoff
cases.rationale: NoDays 10 > cutoff 9.5 is true, so the extra month is added. A port that truncates the cutoff to an integer (9) also adds it, but one that rounds or casts it wrongly may not.

response.notes:
The port follows the source and the spec. I traced two of the golden cases by hand (e-8b16f38f7228, the March DST cutoff case, and e-1906c08077a7) and they match. I did not run the module against the full set of golden cases.

Assumptions I couldn't confirm from the source:
- Ambiguous and nonexistent local times. I assumed PostgreSQL always takes the later UTC instant. My port tries both fold values and keeps the later result. For a nonexistent time (spring forward) that means the pre-change standard offset; for an ambiguous one (fall back) it means standard time.
- Fractional days. Days are added as 86400*N seconds: an exact Decimal product, then converted to float, multiplied by 1e6 and rounded half-to-even to whole microseconds. I believe this matches how PostgreSQL rounds interval * float8.
- NoDays. This is the whole-day part of the elapsed microseconds between the two dates, truncated toward zero. That is my model of justify_hours followed by EXTRACT(day).
- Month offset. FixMonthOffset is truncated toward zero with int(Decimal). When adding months, the local wall-clock time is kept and the day is clamped to the end of the month. The cutoff month is added as a separate step, so clamping can happen twice.
- IsDueFixed. Trailing spaces are stripped before comparing, matching how PostgreSQL compares character(1). Otherwise only an exact 'Y' selects the fixed branch.
- More than one matching row. The last row wins, as in the legacy loop. In practice there can't be more than one because the column is the primary key.
- NULL docdate returns None.
